column1: # Tips for `dot tip` and the startup card. One per line, tab-separated:
#   id    used-when (extended regex on your shell history, or - when it can't be seen there)    tip
# A tip whose regex matches something you ran in the last 90 days counts as
# known and is skipped. Keyboard shortcuts can't be seen in history (-): they

column3: dot recall 5173 finds anything a command printed, even in a tab you closed (--ai "what port did the api use?")
dot night "api: fix the flaky test" queues a task; Claude works on it at 01:30 in its own worktree
dot habits turns the long commands you keep typing into short aliases
dot standup writes yesterday / today / blockers from your commits, PRs and notes — copied, ready to paste
dot note "client approved the mockups" — notes end up in standups and client updates
dot update acme writes this week's client update from the work in their repos
dot mode share acme before a client call: bigger font, other projects hidden, no notifications
dot invite gives someone a read-only browser link to a terminal tab (QR code included)
dot try owner/repo opens any repo in a locked-down container, with a tour and a red-flag check
dot janitor frees the disk space old projects sit on (node_modules, caches, old images)
dot save-game NAME keeps a workspace's tabs, splits and programs — dot load-game NAME after a reboot
dot new portal --client acme starts a project from Kaine Forge: repo, CI, AI setup, workspace
dot ports shows what's listening and which project it belongs to — dot ports kill 5173
dot name gives this repo's dev server https://<repo>.localhost with a trusted certificate
dot wrapped: your week as a card — time per project, top commands, agent hours
dot sync-history shares your shell history between your machines (end-to-end encrypted)
dot evolve: once a week Claude fixes the dotfiles where you struggled and opens a draft PR
right after a command fails, ai fix reads the error on screen and suggests the fix
ai explain 'tar -xzvf x.tgz' explains any command, flag by flag
ai "find files over 100MB here" turns plain English into a shell command (asks before running)
rgf "TODO" searches every file and opens the hit in Neovim at that line
y opens the yazi file manager; quit it and your shell is in the folder you were looking at
z api jumps to the folder you use most that matches "api" — z <Tab> shows a menu
tldr tar: the five examples you need instead of the whole man page
a justfile in a repo + just = the project's commands with Tab completion
xh POST api.dev/users name=ana — curl for APIs, readable both ways
… | fx opens JSON in an explorer you can fold and search
git undo takes back the last commit and keeps its changes
git recent lists the branches you touched lately, newest first
lazygit: stage lines, split commits and rebase with the keyboard
Leader Space (Alt+q, Space) labels every URL, path and hash on screen — two keys copy one
Shift+↑ / Shift+↓ jump between commands; Leader y copies the last command's output
Leader a: every Claude Code session, which ones wait for you, and a jump there
Leader ? opens Claude in a side pane that already knows the folder, git state and last output
Leader p opens a project from ~/Github as its own workspace (shell, nvim, lazygit)
Ctrl+Shift+P: command palette — projects, rename tab, save game, edit dotfiles…
Ctrl+G: saved commands with blanks to fill in (adb, docker, kubectl, git…)
Alt+V, speak, any key: push-to-talk turns what you said into an ai command (speech stays local)
after a typo, a 💡 fix shows under the prompt — F1 puts it on the command line
Ctrl+Shift+U: emoji and symbol picker
Ctrl+R searches your whole shell history; → accepts the grey suggestion as you type
z "the mandarin app" jumps to a project by what it is (README, client, commits) when you forget its folder name — dot find lists the matches
